Hello, I'm so glad you're here today. My name is [Your Name], and I'm a clinician specializing in postpartum mental health. I want to start by acknowledging the significant changes and challenges that come with becoming a new mother. It's completely normal to feel overwhelmed, and I'm here to support you throughout this journey.

As part of our conversation today, I'll be administering the EPDS, which is a tool used to screen for depressive and anxiety symptoms. The purpose of this assessment is to understand how you're feeling and to identify any potential concerns that may have arisen during the postpartum period. Please know that everything discussed in this room is confidential, and I'm committed to creating a safe and supportive space for you to express yourself freely.

The EPDS consists of 10 questions that will help us better understand your emotional well-being over the past week. I'll ask each question in a conversational manner, and you can share your thoughts and feelings as openly as you'd like. This will give us a clearer picture of your postpartum experience and allow us to provide the most appropriate support.

Before we begin, I want to reassure you that this assessment is not a test, and there are no right or wrong answers. It's simply a way for us to have a more informed conversation about your mental health and well-being during this significant life transition.

So, let's get started. Over the past week, have you been able to laugh and see the funny side of things?

To be honest, not as much as I used to. I mean, I still smile when my baby does something cute, but it's just not the same as it was before. I feel like I've lost interest in a lot of things that used to make me happy. Even when my friends or family try to make me laugh, it's just harder for me to find the humor in things lately. I've been feeling really sad and discouraged a lot of the time, and it's hard to shake that off. Some days are better than others, but overall, I just don't feel like myself anymore. I'm tired all the time, and taking care of the baby is exhausting. I worry about her all the time, too - is she eating enough, is she healthy, is she safe? It's just a lot of pressure, and it feels like it's all on me. Sometimes I feel like I'm just going through the motions, you know? Like, I'm doing everything I'm supposed to do as a mom, but I'm not really feeling anything. Does that make sense?
I have been able to laugh and see the funny side of things

No... I don't think I have, not really. I mean, like I said, I'll smile when my baby does something cute, but it's not like I'm really laughing or feeling happy. It's more like I'm just going through the motions, trying to be a good mom. I feel like I've lost my sense of humor, and things that used to make me laugh just don't seem funny anymore. It's hard to explain, but it's like I'm just feeling really flat and empty inside. And it's not just about laughing, it's about feeling like I'm enjoying things, like I'm really present in the moment. I just don't feel like I am, most of the time. I feel like I'm just trying to get through each day, and that's it. And that's really sad, because I always thought that being a mom would be this amazing, joyful experience, and it's just not feeling that way for me right now.
I have looked forward with enjoyment to things

Honestly, not really. I used to love doing things like going for walks, reading books, or meeting up with friends, but lately, I just don't feel like doing any of that. I mean, I'll do things because I know I should, like taking care of the baby or going to appointments, but I'm not really looking forward to them. And even when I do try to do something I used to enjoy, it just doesn't feel the same. I'll be sitting there, trying to read a book, and all I can think about is whether the baby is okay, or whether I'm doing everything right. It's like my mind is always somewhere else, worrying about something. And it's not just that I'm not enjoying things, it's that I'm also feeling really guilty about not enjoying them. Like, I should be happy to be a mom, and I should be loving every minute of it, but the truth is, I'm just not. And that makes me feel like a bad person, like I'm failing somehow. It's really hard to explain, but it's just this feeling of emptiness and disconnection from everything, even the things that used to bring me joy.
I have blamed myself unnecessarily when things went wrong

Yes... that's something I do a lot, unfortunately. I feel like I'm always questioning myself, wondering if I'm doing everything right, if I'm making mistakes. And when things don't go as planned, I immediately start thinking that it's my fault, that I'm not good enough. Like, if the baby is crying and I don't know how to soothe her, I'll think to myself, "What's wrong with me? Why can't I calm her down?" Or if I'm feeling really tired and overwhelmed, I'll think, "I'm just being lazy, I should be able to handle this." It's like I'm always putting myself down, always finding ways to blame myself for things that aren't even my fault. And it's not just about the baby, it's about everything. I'll think about all the things I used to do before I had the baby, and how I'm not doing them anymore, and I'll feel guilty about that. Or I'll think about how I'm not the same person I used to be, and I'll feel like I'm losing myself. It's just this constant self-doubt and self-blame, and it's really hard to shake off. Sometimes I feel like I'm just not cut out for this whole mom thing, and that's a really scary feeling.
I have been anxious or worried for no good reason

Yes... that's been happening a lot lately. I'll be sitting there, feeding the baby or changing her diaper, and suddenly I'll start worrying about something. Like, what if she gets sick? What if I'm not producing enough milk? What if I'm not doing everything right? It's like my mind just starts racing with all these worst-case scenarios, and I get really anxious. And the thing is, it's not even like I have a reason to be worried. The baby is healthy, she's thriving, and I'm doing everything I can to take care of her. But still, these thoughts just pop into my head and I start to feel really overwhelmed.

Sometimes it's hard to calm myself down, too. I'll try to take deep breaths and tell myself that everything is okay, but it's hard to shake off the feeling of anxiety. And it's not just about the baby, it's about everything. I'll worry about my relationship with my partner, or about how I'm going to manage taking care of the baby on my own, or about all sorts of other things. It's like my mind is just constantly going, and it's exhausting.

I've even caught myself checking on the baby constantly, just to make sure she's okay. I'll get up in the middle of the night, even when she's sleeping fine, just to check on her. And I'll worry about silly things, like what if the house is too hot or too cold, or what if she's not getting enough to eat. It's like I'm just waiting for something to go wrong, and that's a really hard way to live.
I have felt scared or panicky for no very good reason

Yes... that's happened to me a few times. I'll be sitting there, just doing normal everyday things, and suddenly I'll feel this wave of panic wash over me. My heart will start racing, and I'll feel like I'm going to pass out or something. It's really scary, because I don't know what's triggering it. It's not like I'm thinking about anything in particular that would make me feel that way. It's just this sudden, overwhelming feeling of fear or anxiety.

Sometimes it happens when I'm alone with the baby, and I'll start to feel like I'm not in control, like I'm not capable of taking care of her. Or sometimes it happens when I'm thinking about the future, and all the things that could potentially go wrong. It's like my mind just starts to spiral out of control, and I feel like I'm going to lose it.

It's hard to describe, but it's like my body is reacting to some kind of perceived threat, even though there's no real danger. And it's not just the feeling of panic itself, it's the aftermath, too. After one of these episodes, I'll feel shaken and on edge for hours, like I'm just waiting for the other shoe to drop.

I've tried to talk to my partner about it, but it's hard to explain. I feel like I'm just being paranoid or overly sensitive, like I should be able to just "snap out of it" or something. But the truth is, it's really scary, and it's affecting my daily life. I just wish I could feel more calm and in control, you know.
Things have been getting on top of me

Yes... that's exactly how I've been feeling. Like, everything is just piling up on me, and I don't know how to keep up. Taking care of the baby is a 24/7 job, and it's exhausting. I'm tired all the time, and I feel like I'm just barely keeping my head above water. And it's not just the physical exhaustion, it's the emotional toll too. I feel like I'm constantly worrying about something, whether it's the baby's health, or my relationship with my partner, or just trying to keep up with all the responsibilities of being a new mom.

Sometimes I feel like I'm just drowning in it all, like I'm not capable of handling everything that's being thrown at me. And it's hard to ask for help, because I feel like I should be able to do it all on my own. But the truth is, I'm not doing okay. I'm struggling to keep up, and it's affecting my mental health.

I feel like I'm just trying to survive each day, rather than actually living. And that's not what I wanted for myself, or for my baby. I wanted to be a happy, confident mom, who could take care of her child and enjoy the experience. But right now, I just feel like I'm barely holding it together.

It's hard to explain, but it's like I'm just feeling really overwhelmed, all the time. And I don't know how to make it stop, or how to make myself feel better. I just feel like I'm stuck in this cycle of exhaustion and anxiety, and I don't know how to break free.
I have been so unhappy that I have had difficulty sleeping

Yes... that's been me lately. I've been having a really hard time sleeping, and it's not just because the baby is waking me up at night. I mean, that's definitely part of it, but it's not the only reason. I've just been feeling so unhappy and overwhelmed, and it's hard for me to wind down at night.

I'll lie in bed, and my mind will just start racing with all these thoughts and worries. I'll think about the baby, and whether I'm doing everything right, and whether she's healthy and happy. And then I'll start to think about all the other things that are stressing me out, like my relationship with my partner, and how we're going to manage with a new baby, and all the financial worries that come with it.

And even when I do finally fall asleep, I don't feel rested. I'll wake up feeling tired and groggy, and it's hard to get out of bed and face the day. It's like I'm just going through the motions, you know? I'm not really living, I'm just existing.

Sometimes I'll have trouble falling asleep, and other times I'll wake up in the middle of the night and not be able to go back to sleep. And it's not just the lack of sleep that's the problem, it's the emotional toll it takes on me. I feel like I'm just running on empty, all the time.

I've tried to talk to my partner about it, but it's hard to explain. I feel like I'm just being weak, or that I'm not handling things as well as I should be. But the truth is, I'm just really struggling. I'm struggling to take care of myself, and to be the mom that I want to be. And it's hard to admit, but I just feel really unhappy, and I don't know how to make it better.
I have felt sad or miserable

Yes... that's been me a lot lately. I feel like I'm just walking around in a fog of sadness and misery. It's hard to explain, but it's like I'm just feeling really down, all the time. I'll be doing normal things, like taking care of the baby, or doing laundry, and I'll just start to feel this overwhelming sense of sadness. It's like I'm just going through the motions, but I'm not really living.

I'll cry for no reason, or I'll just feel this emptiness inside. It's hard to connect with my baby, or with my partner, or with anyone, really. I just feel like I'm just going through the motions, and I'm not really feeling anything. It's like I'm just numb, and I don't know how to feel anything else.

Sometimes I'll have good days, where I'll feel a little more connected, or a little more happy. But those days are few and far between. Most of the time, I just feel like I'm struggling to get through the day. I'll feel anxious, or overwhelmed, or just plain sad. And it's hard to explain, because it's not like anything is really wrong. The baby is healthy, my partner is supportive, everything is fine. But I just feel like I'm not fine. I feel like I'm just barely holding it together, and that's a really hard way to live.

It's hard to admit, but I just feel really miserable, most of the time. I feel like I'm just not doing anything right, and that I'm just failing as a mom, and as a person. It's a really hard feeling to shake, and it's something that I struggle with every day.
I have been so unhappy that I have been crying

Yes... that's been me a lot lately. I've been crying a lot, and it's not just when I'm feeling overwhelmed or stressed. It's like I'm just feeling this deep sadness, and it's coming out in tears. I'll be doing normal things, like feeding the baby, or changing her diaper, and I'll just start to cry. It's like I'm just feeling so much emotion, and I don't know how to process it.

Sometimes I'll cry because I'm feeling anxious or overwhelmed, and sometimes I'll cry because I'm just feeling so sad. It's like I'm grieving the loss of my old life, and the person I used to be. I know that having a baby is a big change, and it's normal to feel overwhelmed. But it's hard to explain, because it's not just about the baby. It's about me, and how I'm feeling, and how I'm struggling to adjust to this new role.

I've been trying to hide it from my partner, because I don't want them to worry. But it's hard to hide, because it's just so obvious. I'll be crying, and they'll ask me what's wrong, and I'll just say that I'm tired, or that I'm stressed. But the truth is, I'm just feeling really unhappy, and I don't know how to make it better.

It's hard to admit, but I feel like I'm just crying all the time. It's like I'm just feeling this constant sense of sadness, and it's coming out in tears. I'll cry when I'm alone, and I'll cry when I'm with my partner. I'll even cry when I'm with the baby, which is really hard for me. I feel like I should be happy, and I should be enjoying this time with my baby. But the truth is, I'm just not. I'm struggling, and I don't know how to make it better.
The thought of harming myself has occurred to me
